name: Advanced geothermal
summary: Drilling and reservoir technologies turn underground heat into dependable electricity in places conventional geothermal could not reach.
useCase: A data centre signs an around-the-clock power contract with a geothermal plant; nearby factories can also buy useful heat.
whyNow: The decisive change is repeatable drilling and reservoir engineering. Fervo reported a 70% reduction in its fastest horizontal-well drilling time between its 2022 Project Red well and a deeper Cape Station well in 2024. In September 2026 its first Cape Station block reached contractual commercial operation at 33 MW. Eavor delivered first grid power at Geretsried in December 2025, demonstrating a different closed-loop approach. These are meaningful project milestones, but they do not establish global cost competitiveness or long reservoir life. The IEA’s large resource estimates are conditional economic potential, not orders or expected installed capacity. Count commissioned power, sustained output and delivered cost separately from memoranda and land leases.

mainstream.scope: Routine procurement of next-generation geothermal power in selected US and European electricity markets with suitable geology and firm-power demand.
mainstream.rationale: The first commercial projects now support a late-2020s replication cycle. Repeat wells, reliable multi-year production and financeable contracts could make selected projects routine early in the 2030s. Permitting, induced seismicity, reservoir decline or disappointing drilling costs could delay adoption beyond this window. IEA’s possible 80% cost decline by 2035 is conditional, not a guaranteed learning curve.

metric.name: Fastest cited Fervo horizontal well: drilling duration
metric.scope: Technology-performance proxy, not market adoption; different well generations and depths.
metric.limitations: 2022 is implied by the issuer’s 70% reduction to 21 days. These are selected fastest wells, not an average, and the 2026 well was substantially deeper. A flat duration can therefore coincide with improving drilling capability. Do not calculate adoption CAGR.
metric.futureNote: No defensible comparable external deployment forecast found. The separate maturity path is an analyst scenario, not measured adoption.
metric.growthLabel: 70% less drilling time in 2024 than the 2022 benchmark

milestones.text: No comparable annual next-generation deployment measurement was identified; early development predates the commercial milestones below.
Fervo drilled the first Project Red horizontal well; it is the baseline for its later drilling-time comparison.
Project Red provided the development platform for the subsequent Cape Station well design; a harmonised global deployment series remains unavailable.
Fervo reported its fastest Cape Station well at 21 days, 70% below the 2022 Project Red drilling benchmark.
Eavor reported first electricity to the German grid from its Geretsried closed-loop project on 4 December.
Fervo reported 33 MW net output and contractual commercial operation for Cape Station’s first GeoBlock on 1 October; the other two initial blocks were still commissioning.

tailwinds: Corporate demand for firm electricity makes bankable long-duration offtake possible.
Oilfield drilling equipment and skills can transfer into geothermal projects.
Modular surface plants and repeated well designs may shorten successive builds.
bottlenecks: Reservoir performance must persist for years, not just a short flow test.
Deep wells, financing, grid access and permits can dominate delivered cost.
Seismicity and water management depend on the geology and technology chosen.
watchMetrics: Net MW that have reached contractual commercial operation, plus actual annual generation and availability.
Median cost and days per completed well at comparable depth, rather than a selected record.
Signed power contracts versus projects that have reached financing and construction.
